strings.name: Brian Kernighan
strings.summary: Born in Toronto and trained in engineering at Toronto and Princeton, Kernighan spent decades at Bell Labs researching Unix tools and software. He coauthored The C Programming Language with Ritchie and worked on AWK, AMPL and combinatorial optimization. His contributions include clear technical writing and practical tools, rather than the design of C. He joined Princeton in 2000 and continued writing textbooks, maintaining tools and teaching computational thinking.

strings.influence.rationale: Contributed to Unix tools and programming-language research, promoting the global spread of C and software practice through writing and education.

strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: University of Toronto engineering bachelor’s degree (1964); Princeton electrical engineering doctorate (1969).
strings.highlights.h1.title: Spreading programming knowledge
strings.highlights.h1.text: Coauthored The C Programming Language with Dennis Ritchie, helping spread C programming practice.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Tools and algorithms
strings.highlights.h2.text: Worked on AWK, AMPL and combinatorial optimization, connecting concise tools with practical problems.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Second edition of the AWK book
strings.timeline.t1.text: Updated the textbook with Aho and Weinberger, covering language evolution and modern data processing.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Coauthoring a Go textbook
strings.timeline.t2.text: Published The Go Programming Language with Alan Donovan, continuing practice-oriented writing.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Joining Princeton’s faculty
strings.timeline.t3.text: Moved into university computing education after decades at Bell Labs.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Publishing the AWK textbook
strings.timeline.t4.text: Systematically presented the text-processing language with fellow developers Aho and Weinberger.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Coauthoring the C textbook
strings.timeline.t5.text: Published The C Programming Language with Ritchie, explaining the language and programming practice.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Publishing Software Tools
strings.timeline.t6.text: Coauthored the book with P. J. Plauger, demonstrating composable program design.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Doctorate and Bell Labs
strings.timeline.t7.text: Earned an electrical engineering doctorate, then began a long career in computing research.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completing studies in Toronto
strings.timeline.t8.text: Completed undergraduate engineering training before further research at Princeton.
